facts.fact: Shukkeien was created in 1620 by Ueda Soko for the Asano clan and is a strolling garden with central pond, islands and landscape compositions; its 1945 destruction and restoration are described.
facts.excerpt: :"ListItem","position":3,"name":"Shukkeien"}]} {"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"Place","name":"Shukkeien","description":"In 1620, the garden was built by Ueda Soko, a chief retainer of the Asano clan and known as a tea master, as a garden for the villa of the lord of the Asano clan. The garden is said to have been modeled after the world-famous scenic West Lake in China, and was named Shukkeien (Shukukeien) because it depicts the scenery of mountains and rivers, the atmosphere of Kyoto and the deep mountains in a miniature form. The pond dug in the center of the garden is topped with islands
